question: When did the All-India Khilafat Committee pass a resolution declaring that no Muslim should serve in the British-Indian army?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fri Jul 01 1921 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fri Jul 01 1921 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)** is the date when the All-India Khilafat Committee passed a resolution declaring that no Muslim should serve in the British-Indian army.
 
• The Khilafat Movement was a significant political and religious campaign launched by Muslims in British India to influence the British government and to protect the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• The movement was led by prominent leaders such as Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali, who played a pivotal role in rallying Indian Muslims against British rule.
 
• It was closely associated with the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi, which aimed at gaining self-governance and full independence for India.
 
• The resolution was part of a broader strategy to unite Muslims and Hindus in the struggle against colonial rule and to assert their political rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Khilafat Movement eventually declined after the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924.
 
• Despite its decline, the movement had a lasting impact on Indian politics by fostering Hindu-Muslim unity and contributing to the broader struggle for Indian independence.
 
• The movement also highlighted the importance of religious and cultural issues in the anti-colonial struggle and set the stage for future collaborations between different communities in India.
